Chapter notes on river deltas: sediment settles where flow slows; farmers built levees long before engines existed. Each season the color of the water changes with upstream rain, and the ferryman keeps a ledger of crossings by lamp-light. Tin roofs hum when hail arrives from the west; the postman counts letters twice on foggy mornings. A cart of glass bottles rattles past the mill at dusk, and dogs bark at nothing in particular. Ledgers, almanacs, tide tables - the clerk copies columns with a blunt nib. Nothing here is about codes, keys, or records of access.
